findings.text: _reviewed_run_refused_the_round suppresses a same-round retry only when the reviewed run's manifest text contains the exact round-token line 'Repair round: <round_id>'. The round token is the advice's first line, so a worker that refuses by quoting the scope line or the blocker prose but not that opening line reads as a mid-work death, and the retry re-sends the identical advice into the same dead end — Defect A's symptom, narrowed rather than closed. The guard degrades toward the retry on an unreadable or non-terminal manifest, which is the safe direction, and any refusal of advice composed after this change quotes the token, so the risk is a worker that paraphrases its refusal. No test exercises a token-less refusal manifest, so the residual is unmeasured.

Two hand-typed resume doors still write the bare advice to resume-<turn>-advice.txt as the launcher's prompt_path: reckon/mcp.py:4670 and reckon/cli.py:5379. Neither restates the time fence, so a repair resume driven through `reckon crew resume` or the MCP surface leaves the worker reading the inherited session's first-attempt deadline — the same door the resumption._resume fix just closed, on a path the automatic repair does not use. The manifest discloses both, with paths, under follow_ons; they are outside this node's write scope.
